evidence: Injected a lost return message after a durable result commit in a throwaway repository bound to the live mechanism (python3 -I lost_callback_injector.py, exit 1) and ran 12 unittest cases (python3 -I -m unittest discover, 12 tests OK). Observed: scan_recovery classified the unit RESUME_OR_RERUN_FROM_IMMUTABLE_INPUT with ingested=false, zero ingestion records, and no reference anywhere in the recovery state to the committed result commit, while the committed result document stayed byte-exact and readable by immutable object id at 1804 bytes; false_completion_count was 0 and verify_chain returned no errors. The hypothesis is refuted: the live scanner does not replay a lost callback from durable state, so recovery of committed results is 0 percent on this path. A repair candidate (repair_candidate_replay_scan.py) enumerates committed result.json documents from Git and ingests each exactly once through the unmodified ingest_result; its tests show PARENT_INGESTED on first replay, ALREADY_INGESTED_NO_REPLAY on the second, refusal of a stale fence, and no COMPLETED state ever set.
falsifiable_hypothesis: A lost return message is replayed from durable state rather than losing the result.
limitations: The defect tests assert the current failing behaviour of the unmodified mechanism, so they will fail by design once a coordinator adopts the repair candidate into workstreams/po03/tools/.
The injection runs against throwaway repositories created per test; it does not exercise a multi-machine provider transport, only the durable custody surface.
provider_run_id is NOT_SUPPORTED because this runtime exposes no subagent spawn tool and therefore no separate provider run identifier.
